check: SELECT d.botdetreg, d.instdateval, (CURRENT_DATE - d.instdateval) AS robot_age_days FROM robot_details d
note: Per robot. installation_date = robot_details.instdateval (date, no nulls, 2022-05-27..2024-11-11); date minus date gives integer days.

from: actuation_data a JOIN robot_details d ON d.botdetreg = a.actrecref
check: SELECT a.actreg, a.actrecref, a.payloadwval, d.payloadcapkg, (a.payloadwval / NULLIF(d.payloadcapkg, 0)) AS pur FROM actuation_data a JOIN robot_details d ON d.botdetreg = a.actrecref
note: Per actuation record (one per operation). actual_payload_weight = actuation_data.payloadwval (kg; null in ~52% of rows); payload_capacity_kg = robot_details.payloadcapkg (3..200 kg). Join actuation_data.actrecref = robot_details.botdetreg (or via operation.operrecref; the routes agree). payloadival is payload inertia, not weight.
checked: ran, 1,000 rows, 52% of them null, from 0.0 to 12.04

from: performance_and_safety p JOIN actuation_data a ON a.actreg = p.effectivenessactuation JOIN operation o ON o.operreg = a.actoperref
check: SELECT p.effectivenessactuation, o.totopshrval, p.emergencystopcount, (o.totopshrval / NULLIF(p.emergencystopcount, 0)) AS mtbs_hours FROM performance_and_safety p JOIN actuation_data a ON a.actreg = p.effectivenessactuation JOIN operation o ON o.operreg = a.actoperref
note: Per actuation/operation record. total_operational_hours = operation.totopshrval (hours, 1087..49921, null in ~half of rows); emergency_stop_count = performance_and_safety.emergencystopcount (0..5). check: SELECT jc.jcondid, jc.jcdetref, ((jc.joint_health->'J1'->>'temperature_C')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J2'->>'temperature_C')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J3'->>'temperature_C')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J4'->>'temperature_C')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J5'->>'temperature_C')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J6'->>'temperature_C')::real) / 6.0 AS avg_joint_temp_c FROM joint_condition jc
note: J1_temp..J6_temp = joint_condition.joint_health->'Jn'->>'temperature_C' (degrees C, 20..80, no nulls). One joint_condition row per operation (jcondoperref), robot = jcdetref. mechanical_status.component_status->'gearboxes' also has temperature_C per joint (gearbox temps); joint_health is the joint reading used here.

check: SELECT jc.jcondid, jc.jcdetref, ((jc.joint_health->'J1'->>'vibration_mmps')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J2'->>'vibration_mmps')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J3'->>'vibration_mmps')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J4'->>'vibration_mmps')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J5'->>'vibration_mmps')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J6'->>'vibration_mmps')::real) / 6.0 AS avg_joint_vibration_mmps FROM joint_condition jc

note: Per controller reading (one per actuation record; systemoverseeroperation links to operation). overseer_load_value = system_controller.overseerloadvalue (CPU load %, 0..100); memory_usage_value = system_controller.memuseval (%, 0..100). No nulls.

note: Incidents per 1000 operating hours, per actuation/operation record. collision_count = performance_and_safety.collisioncount, zone_violations = zoneviolnum, speed_violations = speedviolnum; total_operational_hours = operation.totopshrval (null for ~half the rows -> NULL rate).

note: positional_error_mm = actuation_data.poserrmmval (mm, 0.001..0.499, null in ~52%); reach_mm = robot_details.reachmmval (mm, 504..2500). Dimensionless fraction (~1e-6..1e-3).
checked: ran, 1,000 rows, 52% of them null, from 0.0 to 0.0

check: SELECT jc.jcondid, jc.jcdetref, GREATEST((jc.joint_health->'J1'->>'temperature_C')::real, (jc.joint_health->'J2'->>'temperature_C')::real, (jc.joint_health->'J3'->>'temperature_C')::real, (jc.joint_health->'J4'->>'temperature_C')::real, (jc.joint_health->'J5'->>'temperature_C')::real, (jc.joint_health->'J6'->>'temperature_C')::real) - LEAST((jc.joint_health->'J1'->>'temperature_C')::real, (jc.joint_health->'J2'->>'temperature_C')::real, (jc.joint_health->'J3'->>'temperature_C')::real, (jc.joint_health->'J4'->>'temperature_C')::real, (jc.joint_health->'J5'->>'temperature_C')::real, (jc.joint_health->'J6'->>'temperature_C')::real) AS joint_temp_diff_c FROM joint_condition jc

check: SELECT jc.jcondid, jc.jcdetref, 0.6 * (((jc.joint_health->'J1'->>'vibration_mmps')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J2'->>'vibration_mmps')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J3'->>'vibration_mmps')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J4'->>'vibration_mmps')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J5'->>'vibration_mmps')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J6'->>'vibration_mmps')::real) / 6.0) + 0.4 * (((jc.joint_health->'J1'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J2'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J3'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J4'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J5'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J6'->>'backlash_deg')::real) / 6.0) AS mech_wear_score FROM joint_condition jc

from: performance_and_safety p JOIN robot_details d ON d.botdetreg = p.effectivenessrobot

Disaster-relief/humanitarian definition; this database is about industrial robots and has no funds utilisation, budget allotment or resource-gap columns.

note: performance_and_safety.calibstateval is character(1): 'Y' Success, '0' (zero, a string) Failed, 'N' Pending.
Disaster-relief/humanitarian definition; this database is about industrial robots and has no supply stocks or population. Depends on [3], which is also not realisable.

note: Fault Prediction Score = maintenance_and_fault.faultpredscore (0..1; NULL in 272 of 513 rows -> no tier). Boundaries 0.3 and 0.7 inclusive in Medium. High tier alone: m.faultpredscore > 0.7.

expression: CASE WHEN p.conditionindexval > 0.9 THEN 'Excellent' WHEN p.conditionindexval >= 0.7 THEN 'Good' WHEN p.conditionindexval >= 0.5 THEN 'Fair' WHEN p.conditionindexval < 0.5 THEN 'Poor' END
check: SELECT CASE WHEN p.conditionindexval > 0.9 THEN 'Excellent' WHEN p.conditionindexval >= 0.7 THEN 'Good' WHEN p.conditionindexval >= 0.5 THEN 'Fair' WHEN p.conditionindexval < 0.5 THEN 'Poor' END AS tier, count(*) FROM performance_and_safety p GROUP BY 1
note: Condition Index = performance_and_safety.conditionindexval (0..1). Shared boundaries 0.9/0.7/0.5 assigned to the higher tier except 0.9, which is Good (Excellent is strictly > 0.9).

Public Health Risk Score is a disaster-relief concept; this robot database has no disease-risk or health-capacity data. (Its stated dependency on [19] Health Degradation Rate is a robot metric, unrelated.)

note: CPU load = system_controller.overseerloadvalue, already in percent (0..100).
Response Effectiveness Score and Coordination Quality Index are disaster-relief operation metrics; neither exists here ([14] is not realisable; its dependency on [15] Average Backlash is unrelated).

check: SELECT count(*) AS n, count(sc.cabhumiditylevel) AS with_humidity, count(CASE WHEN substring(sc.cabhumiditylevel from '[0-9.]+')::real < 60 THEN 'Safe' WHEN substring(sc.cabhumiditylevel from '[0-9.]+')::real <= 80 THEN 'Warning' WHEN substring(sc.cabhumiditylevel from '[0-9.]+')::real > 80 THEN 'Danger' END) AS classified FROM system_controller sc
note: Cabinet humidity = system_controller.cabhumiditylevel (text, %). It is NULL in every one of the 1000 rows, so no row can be classified in the current data. Workcell Humidity sensors (environmental_readings/environmental_sensors) measure ambient cell humidity, not the control cabinet, and are not substituted.

note: robot_details.payloadcapkg takes only 3,5,10,20,50,100,200 kg: Light = 3/5/10, Medium = 20/50/100, Heavy = 200.

note: Air pressure = performance_and_safety.airpressval, in bar (5.0..7.0). Data never exceeds 7.0, so 'High' never occurs.

check: SELECT CASE WHEN (((jc.joint_health->'J1'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J2'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J3'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J4'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J5'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J6'->>'backlash_deg')::real) / 6.0) < 0.01 THEN 'Low' WHEN (((jc.joint_health->'J1'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J2'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J3'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J4'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J5'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J6'->>'backlash_deg')::real) / 6.0) <= 0.05 THEN 'Medium' WHEN (((jc.joint_health->'J1'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J2'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J3'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J4'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J5'->>'backlash_deg')::real + (jc.joint_health->'J6'->>'backlash_deg')::real) / 6.0) > 0.05 THEN 'High' END AS severity, count(*) FROM joint_condition jc GROUP BY 1
note: Applied to [15] Average Backlash (degrees) per joint_condition row. In the data averages lie ~0.02..0.08, so no row is Low.
Cost Per Person Affected and Response Effectiveness Score are disaster-relief metrics; no such data. (Stated dependency on [5] Average Joint Vibration is unrelated.)

Brake status is held in mechanical_status.component_status->'brakes'->>'J1'..'J6', but its values are only 'Normal', 'Warning', 'Error' (or null). None of the defined codes 'Released', 'Applied', 'Replaced', 'Slipping' occur anywhere in the database, so the meanings cannot be mapped.

check: SELECT o.apptypeval, CASE WHEN o.apptypeval IN ('Material Handling', 'Picking', 'Packing', 'Palletizing') THEN 'Material Handling' WHEN o.apptypeval IN ('Processing', 'Grinding', 'Polishing') THEN 'Processing' WHEN o.apptypeval = 'Assembly' THEN 'Assembly' WHEN o.apptypeval = 'Welding' THEN 'Welding' WHEN o.apptypeval = 'Standby' THEN 'Standby' END AS app_group, count(*) FROM operation o GROUP BY 1, 2

from: actuation_data a JOIN robot_details d ON d.botdetreg = a.actrecref

note: Uses [1]. 8 actuation records qualify; a few have payloadwval far above capacity (PUR up to ~12), likely data errors, but they satisfy the definition.

from: robot_details d JOIN operation o ON o.operrecref = d.botdetreg

from: performance_and_safety p JOIN actuation_data a ON a.actreg = p.effectivenessactuation JOIN operation o ON o.operreg = a.actoperref

from: (SELECT o.operreg, o.operrecref, o.apptypeval, a.payloadwval / NULLIF(d.payloadcapkg, 0) AS pur, 60.0 / o.cycletimesecval AS throughput, NTILE(5) OVER (PARTITION BY o.apptypeval ORDER BY 60.0 / o.cycletimesecval DESC) AS tp_quintile FROM operation o JOIN actuation_data a ON a.actoperref = o.operreg JOIN robot_details d ON d.botdetreg = a.actrecref WHERE o.cycletimesecval > 0) q
check: SELECT q.operreg, q.apptypeval, q.pur, q.throughput, q.tp_quintile FROM (SELECT o.operreg, o.operrecref, o.apptypeval, a.payloadwval / NULLIF(d.payloadcapkg, 0) AS pur, 60.0 / o.cycletimesecval AS throughput, NTILE(5) OVER (PARTITION BY o.apptypeval ORDER BY 60.0 / o.cycletimesecval DESC) AS tp_quintile FROM operation o JOIN actuation_data a ON a.actoperref = o.operreg JOIN robot_details d ON d.botdetreg = a.actrecref WHERE o.cycletimesecval > 0) q WHERE q.pur > 0.8 AND q.tp_quintile = 1
note: Uses [1] and [12]. Quintiles by NTILE(5) over rows with a known cycle time, partitioned by operation.apptypeval (NULL application, 519 of 1000 operations, forms its own partition; add o.apptypeval IS NOT NULL inside the subquery to exclude it), highest throughput = quintile 1.

note: Uses [19]. Since conditionindexval < 1 in all rows, every robot with a condition reading is 'Degrading'.

from: (SELECT d.modelseriesval, SUM(o.progcyclecount) AS total_cycles FROM robot_details d JOIN operation o ON o.operrecref = d.botdetreg GROUP BY d.modelseriesval) m CROSS JOIN (SELECT percentile_cont(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x.total_cycles) AS p75 FROM (SELECT SUM(o2.progcyclecount) AS total_cycles FROM robot_details d2 JOIN operation o2 ON o2.operrecref = d2.botdetreg GROUP BY d2.modelseriesval) x) pc
check: SELECT count(*) AS models, count(*) FILTER (WHERE m.total_cycles >= pc.p75) AS top_tier, min(pc.p75) AS p75 FROM (SELECT d.modelseriesval, SUM(o.progcyclecount) AS total_cycles FROM robot_details d JOIN operation o ON o.operrecref = d.botdetreg GROUP BY d.modelseriesval) m CROSS JOIN (SELECT percentile_cont(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x.total_cycles) AS p75 FROM (SELECT SUM(o2.progcyclecount) AS total_cycles FROM robot_details d2 JOIN operation o2 ON o2.operrecref = d2.botdetreg GROUP BY d2.modelseriesval) x) pc
note: Robot model = robot_details.modelseriesval (585 series); program cycle count = operation.progcyclecount, summed over all operation records of that series' robots.

from: (SELECT sc.systemoverseeractuation, d.botdetreg, d.modelseriesval, (sc.overseerloadvalue + sc.memuseval) / 2.0 AS stress, AVG((sc.overseerloadvalue + sc.memuseval) / 2.0) OVER (PARTITION BY d.modelseriesval) AS series_avg_stress FROM system_controller sc JOIN actuation_data a ON a.actreg = sc.systemoverseeractuation JOIN robot_details d ON d.botdetreg = a.actrecref) s
check: SELECT count(*) AS n, count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.stress > 1.2 * s.series_avg_stress) AS anomalous FROM (SELECT sc.systemoverseeractuation, d.botdetreg, d.modelseriesval, (sc.overseerloadvalue + sc.memuseval) / 2.0 AS stress, AVG((sc.overseerloadvalue + sc.memuseval) / 2.0) OVER (PARTITION BY d.modelseriesval) AS series_avg_stress FROM system_controller sc JOIN actuation_data a ON a.actreg = sc.systemoverseeractuation JOIN robot_details d ON d.botdetreg = a.actrecref) s
note: Uses [6]. Model series = robot_details.modelseriesval; many series have only 1-2 controllers, so a single-controller series can never be anomalous.
